result:
I can't fully verify this from first principles, so my verdict rests partly on the reviewer's claim and partly on a gap I can see in the proposed solution.

The proposed answer assumes the three subgroups have orders $p^{n-1}$, $p-1$, and $p^{n-1}(p-1)$. The last of these is the whole of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, which is cyclic of order $p^{n-1}(p-1)$. The argument never explains why $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ itself should give an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra when its proper subgroups are excluded or included in a specific pattern. Its inclusion looks like an assumption rather than a derived fact. The trivial subgroup (order 1) is also never considered, and it is a natural candidate for a special case. The sum $p^n + p - 1$ is arithmetically correct for the orders the solution chose, so the error, if there is one, lies in the identification of the subgroups.

I don't have a reliable recollection of the exact classification from the literature on Terwilliger algebras of orbit Schur rings over cyclic $p$-groups. So I can't confirm the correct set of orders. Given the unexplained inclusion of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ and the omission of the trivial subgroup, I don't think the answer can be accepted as stated.

VERDICT: REJECT
